newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mediator sees deal on French truckers main demands.
newsitem.headline: Mediator sees deal on French truckers main demands.

text.p: The government mediator chairing talks between striking French truck drivers and employers said on Wednesday that agreement had been reached on their two main demands and talks would continue later in the day.

Robert Cros told reporters in a statement: "During the night, an important agreement was concluded on the two main demands." He said they were retirement at 55 instead of 60 for drivers with 25 years' experience and shorter working hours.

As the strike entered its 10th day, truck drivers were manning more than 200 roadblocks across the provinces, sealing motorways, ports, borders and fuel depots to back their demands for a 10 percent pay rise, shorter hours and early retirement.

Union leaders confirmed that a consensus had been reached on early retirement, to be funded by the government, but said further negotiations were necessary on pay and hours and urged their members to stay on the barricades.
Cros said three of the five trade unions in the talks had signed agreements on three measures with the employers.
After a 20-hour overnight negotiating marathon, talks were set to resume at 4 p.m. (1500 GMT).
